issues.summary: Unclaimed PENDING/RETRY_WAIT receipts could previously transition to terminal state, bypassing the current lease/fence.
A backdated completedAt on an old active receipt could previously permit immediate deletion after completion.
An orphan plus changed the runBrowser declaration into an expression and removed its callable binding.
The evidence needed explicit cross-owner cursor rejection, terminal-session checks, and a logout-versus-lock-wait authorization race.
The global zero-alert assertion included the separate Next.js route announcer in its open shadow root.
The earlier User contract exact index inventory omitted the two newly added Phase012 indexes.
After the valid artifact commit, automatic Git rename detection omitted the deleted login path from the implementation snapshot and caused metadata generation to fail despite unchanged product bytes.
The initial post-artifact recovery guard authenticated old quality/review and archived executors but did not compare every original committed attempt report/artifact with its original Git blob.

dispositions.resolution: Every non-claim state update must originate from a current unexpired RUNNING claim with matching owner/fence. The real database rejects three unclaimed PENDING transitions and both old/current contexts attempting to finish RETRY_WAIT without a fresh claim; fence 3 succeeds after reclaim.

Terminal INSERT and UPDATE normalize completedAt to public.auth_now() and retain the receipt for at least 24 hours from that database time. Real PostgreSQL evidence covers a 48-hour-old active receipt with backfilled completion, immediate deletion rejection, future completion rejection, and normalization of a synchronous terminal INSERT minimum retention.
The function declaration is restored. The final real browser process exits 0 and executes all eight browser cases.

A second authorized administrator cannot reuse the first owner cursor. Real revoked/expired sessions are denied and remain terminal. A PATCH waiting on the actual management advisory lock returns 401 after real logout commits, with zero additional business changes, USER_UPDATE audits, or receipts.

The failure evidence and old browser source are preserved. The final test still injects a real database SELECT failure and verifies 503 followed by recovery to 200, zero management-main alerts, and one separate framework route-announcer alert. Logout then rejects the next protected request with 401.

The exact index inventory conditionally includes only User_createdAt_id_idx and User_role_status_id_idx when the admin model exists, and checks their btree column order. All earlier scalar, enum, email uniqueness, and original index assertions remain. The complete legacy User group now passes 31/31 with no skips.

Implementation inventory now uses git diff --no-renames, retaining the old login path as null and binding the new path contents across Git staging and commit states. The genuine failed artifact, metadata command observation, original scripts and reports are preserved. Formal seven-case acceptance and all 22 supporting checks were rerun; the real Git rename regression passes. The phase start was not reset; the failed artifact must be included in the final Gate recoveryCommits.

The recovery guard now enumerates the complete original attempt directory from the failed artifact with a NUL-delimited recursive Git tree inventory, requires the old frozen plan and all original case reports, and compares all 45 original files against their committed blobs. A changed old case report is rejected even though the quality/review hashes remain unchanged. Later diagnostic and executor archives are separately authenticated; checking the old artifact for absence of a Gate remains compatible with a subsequent current Gate.

limitations.description: Both user-page axe 4.13.0 reports have zero reported violations but one incomplete color-contrast rule: the tool cannot parse oklch(0.985 0 none), targeting an edit button. Zero violations is not a claim of complete contrast verification or overall WCAG compliance.
Keyboard/focus/navigation were automated and screenshots were reviewed; human screen-reader experience was not evaluated.

Rotation checkpoint persistence/reclaim uses a disconnected and reconnected Prisma client. Separate operating-system process restart is demonstrated for user-command replay; no Phase016 rotation worker or provider operation is claimed.

The receipt TRUNCATE negative uses the application role and can be rejected by its ACL. It is not presented as isolated runtime proof of the TRUNCATE trigger; the trigger definition and applied migration bytes were independently reviewed.
Only synthetic isolated PostgreSQL/browser traffic was used. Production identities, external providers, deployment, Phase013 endpoints and Phase016 workers were not evaluated or implemented.
